source.title: AAOIFI Governance Standard (GS) 15: Syndicated Financing
source.approved: 19-20 July 2023 (AGEB meeting no. 31, 1-2 Muharram 1445H), approved unanimously
source.effective_date: Syndicated financing transactions executed on or after 1 July 2024; earlier application encouraged
source.companion_standard: Must be read in conjunction with AAOIFI Shari'ah Standard (SS) 24 'Syndicated Financing' (2005)

display_card.name: GS 15 — Syndicated Financing
display_card.one_liner: Governance framework for the full lifecycle of Shari'ah-compliant syndicated financing — from mandate to maturity — including strict segregation rules for hybrid deals with conventional banks.

applies_to: Those charged with governance and management of the lead arranger
Syndicate participants (IFIs and, in hybrid arrangements, CFIs' Shari'ah tranche counterparts)
The IFI's customers, in their respective capacities
applicability.sukuk_carve_out: Sukuk are excluded from scope, BUT guidance on the awarding-of-mandate phase and transaction-close phase applies mutatis mutandis to listed and unlisted Sukuk issuances insofar as not in conflict with GS 12 'Sukuk Governance' (para 6)
applicability.customer_binding: Customer is bound to Shari'ah principles and this standard by virtue of signing the mandate and transaction documents (BC22)

seven_principles: Effective Shari'ah compliance structures (minimum: comply with SS 24)
Fair treatment of and amongst stakeholders
Equitable and fair treatment amongst syndication participants (fees commensurate with work)
Effective oversight by lead arranger's governance organs
Transparency and mutual disclosures at all stages
Code of conduct and ethics (AAOIFI code of ethics + IFSB conduct-of-business principles)
parties: Facility agent (optional, roles left to mutual agreement)

key_documents.mandate: First document; initiates syndication, sets proposed terms, exclusivity, customer's Shari'ah-compliance commitment, authorises arrangers (para 16)
key_documents.provisional_fatwa: Initial Fatwa from lead arranger's SSB approving the basic structure — enables documentation drafting and gives other SSBs early comfort (paras 7(k), 17)
key_documents.information_memorandum: Minimum contents listed in para 23 (a-r): customer profile, feasibility study, pricing, profit/loss-sharing ratios, fees, risks, credit assessment, settlement mechanisms, credit enhancements, dispute resolution, etc.
key_documents.inter_financier_agreement: Term deliberately chosen over 'inter-creditor agreement' (BC15). Minimum contents in para 25 (a-m): rights/responsibilities, security handling per Shari'ah, equitable-treatment terms, information protocols, pre-exit conditions, transfer of shares, dispute resolution. No illustrative format included — IIFM has a documentation project (BC6-BC7)

key_rules_for_assurance: Minimum Shari'ah bar: every syndicated transaction must comply with SS 24 plus any other applicable Shari'ah standards (Principle 1)
Provisional Fatwa from lead arranger's SSB required at mandate stage (para 17)

Hybrid arrangements: Shari'ah tranche sanctity maintained at all times; arrangers of the Shari'ah tranche must be IFIs only; IFI may NOT lead, arrange or facilitate (incl. as agent) the conventional tranche in any manner (para 21)
Hybrid arrangements: TWO distinct inter-financier agreements — one for the Shari'ah tranche, one for the conventional tranche; IFIs must not sign the combined one (paras 26-27, BC16-BC18)

Hybrid entry conditions: overall purpose Shari'ah-compliant, AND either (a) IFIs alone cannot meet the need and the customer alone approaches CFIs, or (b) a CFI already holds the mandate and a separate Shari'ah tranche is created with SSB approvals (para 20)
Conflict of interest at mandate: transparent negotiation, disclosure of prior relationships/exposures/off-market fees, refusal of mandate if interests would be jeopardised (paras 18-19)
Transaction close: lead arranger discloses allocation basis, preferential allocations, underwriting details to customer (para 31); customer given reasonable time to evaluate contracts (para 32)
Non-participating invitees must not counter-propose directly to the customer or divulge non-public information (para 37)
Continuity: each participant remains responsible for Shari'ah compliance of its own proportionate share — own SSB, Shari'ah compliance function, internal + external Shari'ah audit (para 40)
Shari'ah issues found by any participant go to lead arranger, who informs all after consulting customer; participants collaborate on a solution (para 41)
Change of Fatwa by any participant's SSB: follow SS 29 and relevant GS, promptly inform all parties, collaborate on Shari'ah-compliant solution (para 42)
Early settlement requires SSB approval of modus operandi, due deliberation, fair treatment (paras 43-44)
Pre-exit by a participant: comply with inter-financier agreement, debt-sale Shari'ah rules where a debt exists, inform customer/participants, NOC and NDA if required (paras 45-46)
Restructuring/rescheduling: must preserve original objective and initial equilibrium of benefits; reviewed and approved by respective SSBs (paras 48-49)
At maturity: SSBs supervise liquidation where needed (paras 50-51)
implications: Creates the first globally standardised governance (not just fiqh) framework for Islamic syndications — SS 24 covered Shari'ah rules; GS 15 adds control, transparency and conflict-of-interest machinery
Hybrid deals are permitted but deliberately discouraged and boxed in — the market signal is 'IFI-only syndicates preferred' (BC10-BC12)
No common/joint SSB per transaction: each IFI's SSB keeps full responsibility; delegation possible but accountability never transfers (BC8-BC9)
The customer — usually not an IFI — is pulled into the compliance perimeter contractually via the mandate (BC20-BC22)
Mandate-phase and close-phase rules leak usefully into Sukuk practice via para 6, filling gaps GS 12 does not cover (BC3)
limitations: No prescribed format for the inter-financier agreement — left to regulators/IIFM/market practice (footnote 6, BC5-BC7)
Facility agent's roles not separately defined — left to mutual agreement of participants (para 7(c), BC23-BC24)
CFIs are not bound by the standard, so in hybrid deals compliance leverage exists only over the IFI side (BC10)

Exception to the two-agreement rule in hybrids possible via a jurisdiction's central Shari'ah board or an SSB case-by-case (e.g. legal enforceability), but the standard itself refuses to codify that exception (BC19)
disputes: Common SSB / shared Shari'ah functions per transaction: proposed for cost and speed, rejected as administratively unworkable and contrary to SSB accountability under existing GSs and regulation (BC8-BC9)
Whether IFIs should be banned from hybrid syndications entirely: rejected; allowed under strict conditions due to industry needs (BC10-BC12)
Terminology fight: 'inter-creditor agreement' rejected to avoid implying Islamic finance is credit/borrowing (BC13-BC15)
Single vs. segregated inter-financier agreement in hybrids: Shari'ah Committee forced segregation late in drafting (2023 amendments) to remove cooperation-in-riba concerns (BC16-BC18, H7)
How far to impose duties directly on the (non-IFI) customer: resolved by keeping the onus on IFIs and binding the customer via contract (BC20-BC22)

timeline_bridge.context: Modern standard. AGEB project approved 29-30 March 2021; exposure draft 29 December 2021; four public hearings 2022; Shari'ah Committee review June + October 2023; final approval July 2023; issued 28 December 2023; effective 1 July 2024.
timeline_bridge.predecessor: AAOIFI SS 24 'Syndicated Financing' (2005) — the fiqh layer this governance layer sits on
timeline_bridge.note_for_app_timeline: Anchor as 2023 issuance / 2024 effectiveness in the contemporary standards era; no classical-period dating applies

related_standards: GS 12 Sukuk Governance (mandate + close phases apply to Sukuk mutatis mutandis)
SS 29 Stipulations and Ethics of Fatwa in the Institutional Framework (change-of-Fatwa procedure)
SS 59 Sale of Debt (relevant to pre-exit where debt is sold)
AAOIFI Code of Ethics for Islamic Finance Professionals
IFSB guiding principles on conduct of business
GS [ED] Shari'ah Decision-Making Process (referenced for Fatwa change, still exposure draft at issuance)
